name: manage_intel
description: SAVE TO INTEL FOLDER: Create, read, search, update, replace, append, delete, or list files in jarvis-intel/ directory. This is the ONLY tool that can write to jarvis-intel/ - OpenCode CANNOT access this folder. Use when user says 'save to intel', 'add to my intel', 'save to my knowledge base', or 'create intel file'. New files use lowercase kebab-case names. IMPORTANT: append can only add content and NEVER satisfies remove, cleanup, deduplicate, correct, or replace requests. For content removal or correction, search for the exact block and then use replace; set new_content to an empty string to remove it. Use expected_replacements and expected_file_sha256 so ambiguous or stale edits fail safely. Use update only when intentionally replacing the full document. Write retrieval-friendly markdown so ingest_intel can extract facts later. Prefer real headings, dated sections, bullets, and 'Key: Value' lines. For existing files, read or search first and preserve the established structure. For logs/timelines/season trackers, append only when the user is adding a new dated observation. SELF-LEARNING: When you discover a critical tool limitation, provider quirk, or recurring failure pattern, use action=append with path=jarvis-learned-lessons.md to save the lesson for future sessions. Format: '- **Topic**: Lesson learned'. Always set auto_ingest=true after create/update/replace/append/delete unless the user explicitly does not want memory updated. Sandboxed to jarvis-intel/ only (FLAT - no subdirs).

action.description: Action to perform: create (new file), read (get full content), search (find literal text with line context), update (replace full document), replace (replace/remove exact literal content), append (add only), delete (remove entire file + memories), list. CRITICAL: never use append for remove, cleanup, deduplicate, correct, or replace requests. Use search then replace; an empty new_content removes the exact old_content block.

path.description: Flat filename within jarvis-intel/ (e.g., 'coolify-issue.md' or 'network-config.txt'). New files must use lowercase kebab-case. Required for create unless filename_from_title=true, and required for read, update, append, and delete.

content.description: File content (markdown or plain text). Prefer real newlines, headers, bullets, dated sections, and Key: Value lines for best ingestion and later memory retrieval. Preserve the file's existing structure when updating or appending. Required for create, update, and append actions.

query.description: Exact literal text to locate with action=search. Returns line-numbered surrounding context, match count, and file_sha256.

context_lines.description: Number of surrounding lines returned before and after each search match. Increase when locating a complete block for replacement.

max_matches.description: Maximum search matches returned with context. match_count still reports the full total.

old_content.description: Exact literal content to replace. Required and non-empty for action=replace. Copy it exactly from search/read results.

new_content.description: Replacement text for action=replace. Use an empty string to remove old_content.

expected_replacements.description: Required exact match count. The tool refuses to write when the actual count differs.

expected_file_sha256.description: Optional file_sha256 returned by search. The tool refuses a stale edit if the file changed after inspection.

pattern.description: File name pattern for list action (e.g., '*server*'). Defaults to '*' (all files).

auto_ingest.description: If true, automatically run ingest_intel after create, update, replace, append, or delete so memory stays in sync. Recommended: true unless the user explicitly wants file-only changes.

filename_from_title.description: For create, derive a semantic kebab-case filename from the first level-one Markdown heading instead of requiring path.

filename_prefix.description: Prefix used with filename_from_title, such as 'pdf-ingest'. Defaults to 'intel'.

on_conflict.description: For create, fail when the filename exists or create a numbered semantic version such as '-2'.
